chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

When a mouse falls into the butter (clarified animal fat) and dies in it, if it was solid, then throw it out and what is adjacent to it, and eat what remains; and if it was melted, then do not eat it and kindle the lamp with it; and oil is similar to that.

key_terms.اسْتَصْبَحْ بِهِ: Use it for lighting lamps (literally: make it a source of light for the morning)
key_terms.الزَّيْت: Oil, typically vegetable or olive oil
key_terms.السَّمْن: Clarified animal fat, typically butter or ghee

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on eating butter or oil if a mouse dies in it?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi outlines the fiqh of impurity (najāsah) regarding a dead mouse in fat, distinguishing between solid and liquid states based on the principle of whether the impurity's essence transfers. It reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on practical purity laws, where solid fat allows for selective removal of the contaminated portion, while melted fat renders the entire mass impure, though it remains permissible for non-consumptive uses like lighting lamps.
